title: Scales of Measurement: Nominal, Ordinal, Interval, Ratio
summary: Four levels of measurement; properties of each scale; examples in psychological testing; implications for statistical analysis.
objectives: Define nominal, ordinal, interval and ratio scales.
Identify permissible statistics for each scale.
revision: NOIR scales: Nominal (categories), Ordinal (rank), Interval (equal intervals), Ratio (true zero). Permissible statistics depend on scale.
traps: Ratio scale = true zero (can compute ratios).
confusions: Confusing interval with ratio (lack of true zero).

notes.t: The scale of measurement determines which statistical operations are meaningful. Nominal data support counting and mode; ordinal data support ranking and median; interval data support mean and standard deviation; ratio data support all operations including ratios.
UGC NET frequently asks to identify the scale of measurement for a given variable and the permissible statistics.

mnemonics.title: NOIR
mnemonics.text: N — Nominal, O — Ordinal, I — Interval, R — Ratio
